summary.text: A 2000 Bulletin feedback piece reporting on how adverse events following immunization were monitored in vaccine trials recorded in the WHO Vaccine Trial Registry. It notes that early-phase trials are too small to detect rare side-effects, defines adverse events according to Good Clinical Practice guidelines, and reviews 68 trials of vaccines against diseases such as cholera, hepatitis B, measles and typhoid. A closing table classifies the adverse events monitored, from local and mild systemic reactions to death, by short-term versus long-term follow-up.

blocks.title: Table 1. Number of vaccine trials conducting short-term (<4 weeks) and long-term (≥ 4 weeks) monitoring of adverse events following immunization (AEFI), WHO Vaccine Trial Registry, 1987–1999
blocks.content: The table shows how many vaccine trials in the WHO Vaccine Trial Registry (1987–1999) conducted short-term (<4 weeks) and long-term (≥ 4 weeks) monitoring of adverse events following immunization, and how many reported details on the types of AEFI, with percentages of the 68 trials.

blocks.title: Table 2. Number of trials reporting adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) in short-term and long-term monitoring, WHO Vaccine Trial Registry, 1987–99
blocks.content: The table shows the number of trials in the WHO Vaccine Trial Registry (1987–99) reporting each type of adverse event following immunization (none, local, mild systemic, immune-mediated, severe systemic toxicity, other, death), separately for short-term (< 4 weeks, n = 17) and long-term (≥ 4 weeks, n = 4) monitoring.
